sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (read in memory with openpyxl read_only; all sheets: Quality Checks row 31, Deterministic Checks, ChangeLogs link, Internal Quality Checks row 31 which has no internal annotation)
evidence:
Workbook row 31 says 'Every / all / only / exactly-one' asks must be checked across the whole collection, and 'unchanged' guards must not punish legitimate side effects. quality-checks.md section 31 adds 'not one sampled row'. The internal sheet has no annotation for this row.

PASSING INSTANCES (whole collection checked):
(1) The 'all of them or none' bulk rule (instruction.md:3; rules:87-92). hro_bulk_all_or_none requires 'none of the set moves' by both UI and replay. hro_bulk_places sends 3 cards into 2 places with Interview empty at B(8), which catches per-card counting. hro_bulk_move checks all three cards' arrival order.
(2) Undo 'puts every card back' (rules:96). hro_undo_restores checks Y, W and X at their places (Y,W,X,Z,A2) and that V stays.
(3) The 'any of those cards' undo blocker (rules:98). hro_undo_conflict changes one card of a multi-card set (X in B10-11, W in B14) and a single card (Z in B15). The non-member control and the note exception (B12, rules:99) keep this guard from punishing legitimate side effects.
(4) hro_activity requires 'every successful board action ... each card of every multi-card move ... every undo', newest first, and the filter must show 'all of that job's lines and only those'. Protocol A lists every protocol it covers (prompt.md:49).
(5) hro_activity_refusals: 'none of the refused attempts'.
(6) hro_candidate_private: 'no response a candidate page receives', with K telling the judge to capture every request and every stream frame (prompt.md:43). Seed check: no candidate's own thread mentions another candidate (APP-101/201/301/302 bodies parsed), so a correct app cannot false-fail on message content.
(7) hro_candidate_view: 'each candidate's own applications all appear'.
(8) hro_thread_latest and hro_thread_earlier: 'most recent 30' and paging 'until none remain'. Both are relative to earlier reviews' messages.
(9) The per-role refusal rows each say 'each refused' over an explicitly listed set: hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_thread_access (Observer, Ingrid and Noor), hro_anonymous (5 requests), hro_job_open (four invalid inputs).
(10) The constraints gate's 'exactly one card'.

'Unchanged' guards: prompt.md:19 says a refused action changes no card, order, message or note. hro_restart is scoped to 'your jobs ...'. hro_unread_counts needs 'exactly two'. These are safe because test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1, so no sibling dimension acts during U or D. The counts are also relative ('rises by'), and polish is told never to use Lena's conversation (polish prompt.md:16). hro_pol_live_thread requires the view to stay at the newest message, so auto-scroll is not punished. hro_pol_live_board fails only on a scroll reset, not on any offset change.

FAILING INSTANCE (universal ask checked on a subset):
- Brief: Observer 'changes nothing' (rules:18,73); 'The board, the Activity view and every staff action are refused to candidates' (rules:194); no session 'reads and writes nothing: 401' (rules:21).
- hro_observer_readonly (functional judge.toml:172-173) and hro_candidate_no_staff (judge.toml:181-182) replay only one single-card move, open-job, add-candidate and note request (prompt.md:45). hro_anonymous (judge.toml:190-191) replays only a board read, a move, add-candidate, note and message.
- No replay covers the multi-card move request, re-order, reject or reopen for these roles. hro_anonymous also has no Activity read and no conversation read.
- hro_mgr_other_job tests only a single move by Bill.
- The golden has a separate multi-card route: src/index.js:339 'app.post('/api/moves/bulk', auth(), ...)' next to :334 single move. Its role check sits in the shared checkMove (:239). So a separate, unguarded bulk path is a natural design that these criteria never probe.

NOTES (not blocking):
(a) B(12) says Mei 're-order a different J2 card (Y) within its stage' with no 'one place' limit. B(14) has that limit. Moving Y to the bottom of Screen would shift A2's place, and an app could arguably treat that as A2 being re-ordered, which would refuse the control undo. Risk is low because Y is at the top and a one-step move does not touch A2. P3.
(b) The undo blocker 'reopened since' (rules:98) has no leg. This is a coverage matter for row 26.
(c) hro_candidate_view lists all six candidate wordings, but protocol K only reaches Application received, In review, Interviewing and Not moving forward. Offer and Hired equal the stage names, so the risk is minimal. This is a coverage matter for row 26.
counterexample: A weak app puts its role guard in the single-card move handler, plus job, candidate and note handlers. Its multi-card move endpoint, POST /api/moves/bulk, checks only that the user is signed in. It also serves GET /api/activity with no session check. The Observer, a candidate, or another job's hiring manager can bulk-move or reject cards on any job, and an anonymous visitor can read the whole Activity log. Under the shipped protocol, the Observer and candidate replays of one single move, open-job, add and note are refused. The anonymous replays of board read, move, add, note and message all return 401. Bill's single move on J1 is refused. So hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous and hro_mgr_other_job all pass, even though the brief says the Observer changes nothing, every staff action is refused to candidates, and no session reads nothing.
suggested_fix: In protocol R, add the captured multi-card move request (and a re-order or reject request when the UI uses a separate request for it) to the Observer, candidate and other-job-manager replays, with Rafael's identical request as the control, and add the Activity read and a conversation read to the anonymous replays, naming them in hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_mgr_other_job and hro_anonymous. Optionally say 'one place' in B(12).
